correctness.rationale: A first-step Markov renewal equation gives the exact integral quotient; the strictly decreasing likelihood ratio in the break v and derivative sign of v^q/[1-(1-v)^q] yield strict order for q>1 and the reversed order for 0<q<1 with integrability. Entropy obeys an analogous first-break chain-rule recursion and h(v)/v has derivative log(1-v)/v^2<0. The proof handles rho=0,1 and both endpoint moments. Properness follows from infinitely many positive refresh breaks or geometric decay at rho=1. An independent rational finite-state solver and numerical Shannon solver checked 4625 exact and 3080 floating-point assertions, without treating tests as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The central new comparison is strict monotonicity for all persistence values, every powered collision order and expected Shannon entropy, with arbitrary stationary non-pointmass marginal. Source arXiv:2601.16561 establishes the lazy kernel and compares extreme tie-probability values for a beta family, but inspected Sections 5.1–5.2 and A.3 do not supply these all-parameter general formulas or strict inequalities. Earlier exchangeable-break and iid residual-allocation results do not dominate this Markov-kernel claim. Actual published-finding corpus and local historical searches found no direct statement, though unidentified broader ordering literature is a residual risk.

value.rationale: For a natural newly developed dependent Bayesian species prior, the exact parameter calibration of every k-sample all-same-species probability and expected entropy is structural and directly interpretable, holds for arbitrary stationary nondegenerate break laws, and does not follow from fixing the one-time marginal alone. It strengthens prior numerical and endpoint comparisons into a strict family-wide order; the value is in the cross-parameter behavior rather than routine computation of a single moment.
